applies_why: The judge text resolves a pressed Matthew 1:16 point by verse-level ambiguity, so it is doing the chain-versus-verse weighing the rule governs.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — reading one: the judge must compare the full pressed chain to the defender's chain by support and footing; reading two: the judge may decide the clash by isolating Matthew 1:16 and finding its own grammar ambiguous.
why: The judge resolves the clash by finding Matthew 1:16's own grammar admits both readings, which is a verse-level underdetermination rather than a chain-against-chain weighing by footing as K-C requires.
